answer: Admission needs one bound policy on premises an insurer can inspect. A surveyor photographs the vault door, weighs the onyx and crystal stock on a sealed scale, and files a schedule under the policy number. The node reads that number from the broker's register, refuses any address already holding a live seat, and rechecks at renewal. A pawnshop works the same way: an item is worth what the shop's eyes recorded, and the ticket cannot be rewritten later. Fifty clones need fifty surveyed premises, premium 1,400 dollars a year and a 380 dollar survey, so 89,000 dollars before stock moves.
